text.p: Copper closed stronger after touching six month highs, taking other base metals with it, while gold remained under pressure overnight.
Oil prices firmed on the back of higher gasoline prices while wheat closed mostly lower.
The CRB index was up 1.58 points at 244.89.
New York precious metals futures ended mixed Tuesday after support levels held following a sharp sell off in the past week.

While some short covering is expected ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday Thursday, the market remains bearish and could yet slide lower, traders said. "The market looks oversold and a bounce was expected today, but it didn't really happen, leaving many people a bit scared," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said. COMEX February gold ended up 60 cents at $376.80, after barely holding above contract lows seen Monday at $375.10. Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $374.70/375.20, after gold was fixed in London Tuesday afternoon at $373.50, its lowest fix since January 9, 1995.

Spot gold closed around $374.50/90 in New York Monday. Fundamentals remain bearish. Concern about European central bank gold sales has been revived in the past few days by reports Switzerland may be going to change its constitution to take the country off its quasi-gold standard which requires gold reserves to be held equal to 40 pct of its currency in circulation.

Copper was the major feature of London Metal Exchange (LME) trading up to Tuesday's close as tight nearby spreads flared on speculative short covering. The all important cash to three months backwardation was last indicated at $240/$250, against Monday's late levels of around $175. Earlier, tomorrow/next day traded at $20, just $3 under the LME limit of $23.
On Monday, margin payments on spread business were doubled to $150 per tonne due to the market tightness.
Three months copper earlier rallied to a six-month high of $2,285 before drifting back to $2,258, up $54 from Monday.

Traders said they expected market conditions to remain choppy near-term. Open interest on $2,600 copper December calls will feature as the closer three months delivery gets to the $2,600 level, the more covering will have to be done.
Copper also found support from a warehouse stock fall of 3,850 tonnes to 6-1/4 year lows of 90,050 tonnes.
Traders are now expecting the market to consolidate before launching an attack on $2,300.

Other metals remained relatively quiet but found support from the uptrending copper market. Aluminium moved towards $1,540 resistance and was last at $1,535, a gain of $22. Nickel after earlier commission house selling bounced back with copper to $7,065, against $6,940. Zinc was at $1,084, up $2 while lead was $5 higher at $714.

Unwinding of bull spreads and profit taking of the December/March spread pressed CBOT wheat futures to a mostly lower close, traders said. "There was a lot of unwinding of the bull spreads getting ready for first notice day. There was a lot of profit taking of the spreads," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. An early drop in the Dow industrial stock index was unnerving to some potential longs, traders said. Wheat closed 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 3/4 higher, with December down 2-3/4 at $4.13.

NYMEX heating oil sharpened losses on a weak cash market where supply was viewed to be adequate, while gasoline remained strong as supplies were tight in the New York Harbor spot market, traders said. Crude was lead higher by gasoline, with January crude rising 15 cents to $23.64 a barrel near the close.
